title: Vesper and the Ember
premise: When prayers in the mountain village of Thornfell begin receiving answers from gods everyone believed dead, August Ravensworth — a runaway apprentice carrying their late hedge-witch mentor's stolen grimoire — discovers the 'answers' are a dying ember-god named Vesper, feeding on faith to survive. The ruling Ashen Conclave wants Vesper's power harvested to fuel their empire, and they'll burn every village that shelters the god. August, a smuggler's daughter named Wren, and a Conclave defector must carry Vesper's last ember across the mountains to the old shrine where gods are reborn — pursued by August's former master, who sold them to the Conclave years ago. At the shrine, August must surrender their own memories of everyone they love to complete the rebirth, and the novel ends with a reborn Vesper choosing to scatter divine power among mortals rather than rule, while August, half-remembering, chooses to stay with the family they found.
about_author: X. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent five years mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. Their work blends folkloric fantasy with quiet, character-driven stories about the families we build when the old ones fail us.

chapters.title: The Road That Answers Back
chapters.summary: August's POV. Fleeing their master's tower with a stolen grimoire, August takes a smuggler's road through Thornfell and stumbles on a shrine where a prayer is audibly answered — impossible, since the gods died centuries ago. The answering voice is weak, frightened, and calls itself Vesper. Beat: uneasy wonder; the world is larger and stranger than August believed.

chapters.title: What the Conclave Burns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Smuggler Wren Hale returns to her home village to find Ashen Conclave inquisitors interrogating worshippers and burning 'god-touched' households. She witnesses a neighbor confess under torture to hearing Vesper. Wren escapes with a Conclave seal stolen from the inquisitor's tent. Beat: cold fury hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Hollow
chapters.summary: August's POV. August returns to Vesper's shrine for answers and finds Wren already there, having tracked rumors of the god. They distrust each other but strike a bargain: Wren will guide them to the rebirth shrine at Mount Cinder's heart; August will share what the grimoire reveals — that the Conclave's founders imprisoned the gods and stole their fire. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Brother Ilen's POV. A Conclave acolyte who has begun hearing Vesper in his prayers deserts the inquisition column, bringing warning: the Conclave has located the shrine's approach and dispatched August's former master, Magister Corvane, to capture the ember. Ilen finds August and Wren and offers his knowledge of Conclave routes. Beat: hope shadowed by betrayal's approach.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: August's POV. In a mountain waystation, August finds evidence Corvane has been tracking them for years — and that their 'runaway' was arranged: Corvane sold August to a patron who wanted a god-touched vessel raised in ignorance. August's memories of a loving mentor curdle. Beat: grief and self-doubt; the past cannot be trusted.

chapters.title: Faith Is a Hunger
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The ember-god, carried in a lantern, confesses the truth: it has been siphoning strength from the villagers' prayers, and the 'miracles' it granted are consuming them — a child lies fevered because Vesper answered too generously. Power, even kindly meant, corrupts. Vesper begs August to promise the ember will be reborn or destroyed. Beat: moral weight settles on the quest.

chapters.title: The Pass of Ashes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvane's hunters ambush the party at a snowbound pass. Ilen holds the line so August and Wren can escape and is captured; Wren, who has begun to love the prickly acolyte, must leave him behind. The ember gutters as Vesper spends itself shielding them. Beat: sacrifice, guilt, and the cost of the road.

chapters.title: The Price of Rebirth
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the shrine's threshold, the grimoire's final page reveals the cost: a rebirth requires a mortal to feed the god their memories of everyone they love — the raw material of a new divine soul. August realizes Corvane always intended them for this, a vessel raised unloved so the sacrifice would be cheap. Beat: despair confronting destiny.

chapters.title: Emberfall
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Corvane arrives with the Conclave's harvest-engine, Ilen a prisoner; he offers August their old life in exchange for handing over the ember. In the battle, Wren's smuggler kin arrive, Ilen breaks free, and August shatters the harvest-engine — but the ember is dying and the shrine is open. August steps forward to pay the price. Beat: climax; choice over coercion.

chapters.title: What Remains of August Ravensworth
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, weeks later. A reborn Vesper, no longer a starving god but a hearth-flame shared freely among villages, keeps watch over August, who lost most memories but kept fragments — a laugh, a name half-remembered, a hand that reaches for Wren's. The Conclave fractures as god-fire spreads beyond its control. Beat: bittersweet resolution; found family endures what memory cannot.
